readings: Treat a and b as two's complement fixed-point words and compute c = a - b directly; e.g. a=0001, b=1111 yields c=0010

Treat the MSB as an independent sign bit and the remaining bits as magnitude, performing separate sign comparison and magnitude add/subtract; the same input vectors produce a completely different c bit pattern
res is combinational (always @(*) / assign) so c is valid in the same cycle as a and b
res is a clocked register (always @(posedge clk)) so c is delayed by one clock cycle relative to a and b
Wrap around: keep only the low N bits of the full-width difference, discarding any carry-out/borrow
Saturate: clamp the result to the most positive or most negative N-bit value when the true difference is out of range
Zero means all N bits equal 0; no additional logic is needed because two's complement zero already has sign bit 0
Zero is detected from the magnitude field only, so a 'negative zero' pattern (sign bit = 1, magnitude = 0) must be explicitly converted to all-zeros, forcing extra output logic
